title: Only 7% Can Pass This Vision Test
summary: Colours, tiny details, patterns, rotations and visual traps get harder across 10 fast rounds.

landing.intro: How sharp are your eyes? Spot tiny differences, track shifting patterns and catch visual traps before they catch you.

about.body:
This visual-perception challenge turns colours, symbols, patterns, spatial turns and hidden details into ten increasingly tricky rounds. Some questions reward a quick scan, while others ask you to slow down, compare two nearly identical records or remember a short visual arrangement.

The quiz is designed for worldwide entertainment and general learning. It measures only how accurately you answer the puzzles shown on your current screen; brightness, display calibration, screen size, viewing distance and surrounding light can all affect what you see.

Your final percentage reflects your answers in this quiz, not the health or quality of your eyesight. A real vision assessment requires appropriate equipment and a qualified eye-care professional.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Study each visual clue and choose the single answer that best matches what is shown.
Correctness stays hidden while you play, so compare carefully before making your selection.
Complete all ten rounds to reveal your Vision Score, strongest visual skill and trickiest area.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment only. This quiz is not an eye examination and cannot diagnose vision conditions.

profiles.title: The Eagle Eye
profiles.copy: You caught subtle shifts that most people would scan straight past. Your focus stayed exceptionally precise as the patterns, rotations and visual traps became harder.

profiles.title: The Visual Virtuoso
profiles.copy: You passed the challenge with a sharp eye for structure, contrast and tiny changes. Even the late-round optical traps rarely pulled your attention off course.

profiles.title: The Pattern Spotter
profiles.copy: You tracked most visual rules confidently and noticed details hidden inside busy displays. A few close comparisons made the focus lab genuinely challenging.

profiles.title: The Detail Detective
profiles.copy: You built a solid result across several kinds of visual puzzle. Your strongest round shows where your attention naturally locks on fastest.

profiles.title: The Focus Finder
profiles.copy: You uncovered plenty of the lab’s hidden clues while discovering which visual traps slow you down. A second look would make many of the missed patterns click.

profiles.title: The Curious Observer
profiles.copy: This set of visual traps found some blind spots, but it also revealed where your focus is strongest. Every missed clue becomes obvious once the underlying rule is exposed.

questions.question: Which tile is a different colour?

visual.ariaLabel: Three blue circles and one violet circle

questions.explanation: The bottom-right tile is violet; the other three are blue.

questions.question: Which code matches exactly?

visual.ariaLabel: Reference code M 7 K 2 P 9

questions.explanation: M7K2P9 matches every letter and number in the reference.

questions.question: What comes next in the pattern?

visual.ariaLabel: Triangle, circle, triangle, circle, unknown

questions.explanation: The pattern alternates triangle and circle, so the next symbol is a triangle.

questions.question: The arrow turns right each time. What comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: Up arrow, right arrow, down arrow, unknown

questions.explanation: A quarter-turn to the right after down points left.

questions.question: Which icon appeared first?
questions.explanation: The star was the first icon in the displayed sequence.

questions.question: How many filled circles are shown?

visual.ariaLabel: Four filled circles and two outline circles

questions.explanation: Four of the six circles are filled.

questions.question: Where is the violet tile?

visual.ariaLabel: A three by three grid with violet in the centre and blue elsewhere

questions.explanation: The only violet tile sits in the centre of the grid.

questions.question: Which pair has the strongest light–dark contrast?
questions.explanation: Black and white create the strongest contrast among these pairs.

questions.question: Which pair creates the clearest colour contrast?
questions.explanation: Blue and orange are far apart in hue, making them easier to distinguish than the more closely related pairs.

questions.question: Which swatch is the warmest colour?
questions.explanation: Orange is the warm colour; blue, green and violet read as cooler here.

questions.question: Which copy changes only one character?
questions.explanation: Q8B6D8 changes only the final character; every other option changes more than one.

questions.question: Which colour was on the right?
questions.explanation: Gold was paired with the right-hand position.

questions.question: Which pair is completely identical?
questions.explanation: Both copies of K4M8P2 contain the same six characters in the same order.

questions.question: Which row contains exactly seven dots?
questions.explanation: The second row contains seven dots.

questions.context:
FIRST: FOCUS — FRAME — FIND
SECOND: FOCUS — FIND
questions.question: Which word disappeared from the second line?
questions.explanation: FRAME appears between FOCUS and FIND in the first line but is missing from the second.

questions.question: Which position contains the changed symbol?

visual.ariaLabel: Three outline diamonds with a filled diamond in the third position

questions.explanation: The third diamond is filled while the others are outlines.

questions.question: Which symbol looks unchanged after a half-turn?
questions.explanation: A circle looks the same after a 180-degree rotation.

questions.context: OFFICE FOCUS: FIND FIVE FLAGS FAST.
questions.question: How many letter Fs are shown?
questions.explanation: OFFICE contains two Fs, and FOCUS, FIND, FIVE, FLAGS and FAST add five more, making seven.

questions.question: Which shape continues the increasing side count?

visual.ariaLabel: Triangle, square, pentagon, unknown

questions.explanation: The shapes have three, four and five sides, so a six-sided hexagon comes next.

questions.question: Which tile completes the alternating row?

visual.ariaLabel: X, O, X, O, X, unknown

questions.explanation: The row alternates X and O, so O completes it.

questions.question: Which arrow completes the rotation?

visual.ariaLabel: Northeast, southeast, southwest, unknown arrow

questions.explanation: Each arrow turns 90 degrees clockwise, making northwest the next direction.

questions.question: What size comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: Small dot, medium dot, large dot, medium dot, small dot, unknown

questions.explanation: The sizes rise to large and then reverse, so medium follows small.

questions.question: Which colour stands out most against deep navy?
questions.explanation: Bright yellow creates the strongest light–dark and warm–cool contrast against deep navy.

questions.question: Which row repeats the reference exactly?
questions.explanation: The fourth row preserves every symbol, fill and position from the reference.

questions.question: Which arrow is the vertical mirror of ↗?

visual.ariaLabel: Northeast arrow reflected across a vertical mirror

questions.explanation: A vertical mirror swaps right and left, turning northeast into northwest.

questions.context: Start in the centre. Move up twice, right once, then down once.
questions.question: Where do you finish relative to the start?
questions.explanation: Two moves up and one down leave one move up; the right move leaves you up-right.

questions.question: Rotate ← clockwise by 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter-turn changes a left arrow into an up arrow.

questions.question: Which symbol stays unchanged in a vertical mirror?
questions.explanation: The vertical double arrow is symmetrical from left to right.

questions.question: Which tile comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: Filled square, two outline squares, filled square, two outline squares, unknown

questions.explanation: Each group starts with one filled square followed by two outline squares.

questions.question: Which object was in the bottom-left position?
questions.explanation: The key occupied the bottom-left position.

questions.question: Which number was paired with blue?
questions.explanation: Blue was paired with the number 7.

questions.question: Which shape came immediately before the star?
questions.explanation: The square appeared directly before the star.

questions.question: Which landmark was east?
questions.explanation: The tower was shown to the east.

questions.question: Which icon was NOT shown?
questions.explanation: The bell, feather and balloon were shown; the anchor was not.

questions.question: Which letter comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: A, C, F, J, unknown

questions.explanation: The jumps increase by one letter each time: plus 2, plus 3, plus 4, then plus 5 from J to O.

questions.question: Which code is unchanged?
questions.explanation: The fourth code matches all six reference characters exactly.

questions.context: THE OTHER THEME HID THE WORD THE.
questions.question: How many standalone instances of THE appear?
questions.explanation: THE appears three times as a standalone word; OTHER and THEME do not count.

questions.question: Which code appears twice?

visual.ariaLabel: Codes A7Q, B4M, C2R and B4M

questions.explanation: B4M appears in both the second and fourth cells.

questions.question: Which position contains the dot inside a circle?

visual.ariaLabel: Four circles with a dot inside the third

questions.explanation: Only the third circle contains a central dot.

questions.question: How many triangles are hidden in the row?

visual.ariaLabel: A row containing four triangles and three other shapes

questions.explanation: Triangles appear in the first, third, fifth and seventh positions.

questions.question: Which centre tile is easiest to spot in the dark cluster?

visual.ariaLabel: Four dark clusters with yellow, violet, blue and green centre tiles

questions.explanation: The yellow centre at top left has the greatest light–dark contrast with the surrounding black tiles.

questions.question: Which direction is the finish from the start?
questions.explanation: The moves cancel to one step up and one step right.

questions.question: Which tile breaks the colour?

visual.ariaLabel: Three green circles and a blue circle in the third position

questions.explanation: The third tile is blue while the others are green.

questions.question: Which code matches exactly?
questions.explanation: V6K9 is identical to the displayed code.

questions.question: What comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: Filled circle, outline circle, filled circle, outline circle, unknown

questions.explanation: Filled and outline circles alternate, so a filled circle comes next.

questions.question: Turn ↓ clockwise once.
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter-turn from down points left.

questions.question: Which icon appeared second?
questions.explanation: The key was the second icon.

questions.question: How many filled stars?

visual.ariaLabel: Four filled stars and two outline stars

questions.explanation: Four of the six stars are filled.

questions.context: Two centre squares carry the same colour code but sit on different backgrounds.
questions.question: Why can the centre squares appear different?

visual.ariaLabel: The same dark centre square shown once against white and once against black

answers: The colour code changes with distance
questions.explanation: Surrounding colours can change perceived contrast even when the centre colours are identical.

questions.context:
VERSION A: FOCUS 2026
VERSION B: F0CUS 2026
questions.question: What changed in Version B?
questions.explanation: The second character changed from the letter O to the numeral 0.

questions.question: Each group doubles its dots. What comes next?

visual.ariaLabel: One dot, two dots, four dots, eight dots, unknown

questions.explanation: The count doubles from one to two to four to eight, so the next group has sixteen dots.

questions.context: The whole page turns, carrying the arrow with it.
questions.question: Where does the arrow point to the viewer now?

visual.ariaLabel: Up arrow, rotate one hundred and eighty degrees, unknown direction

questions.explanation: A half-turn reverses north to south relative to the viewer.

questions.question: Which colour and position were paired?
questions.explanation: Gold was shown in the centre position.

questions.context:
REFERENCE: SIGHT · LIGHT · NIGHT
COPY: SIGHT · L1GHT · NIGHT
questions.question: Which word was altered?
questions.explanation: LIGHT was changed to L1GHT by replacing the letter I with the number 1.

questions.context: Find the pair that changes in two ways: it must shift from light to dark and also move to a clearly different hue.
questions.question: Which pair changes both brightness and hue?
questions.explanation: Pale yellow to deep violet changes from light to dark and crosses to a distinctly different hue; the other pairs mainly change only one of those qualities.

questions.question: Which precise change was made?
questions.explanation: The strings match until the final character, where 4 becomes 9.

questions.context: Shapes alternate circle, square. Fills repeat filled, outline, outline.
questions.question: Which item follows the six shown?

visual.ariaLabel: Filled circle, outline square, outline circle, filled square, outline circle, outline square, unknown

questions.explanation: The next shape is a circle and the fill cycle returns to filled, producing a filled circle.

questions.context: An arrow starts pointing up. Turn it right once, then rotate it 180 degrees.
questions.question: Which direction does it finally point?
questions.explanation: The first turn points east; a further half-turn points west.

questions.question: Where was the triangle, and what colour was it?
questions.explanation: The triangle was in the centre and was paired with gold.

questions.context:
LINE A: A7K2-M9Q4-R6
LINE B: A7K2-N9Q4-R8
questions.question: How many character positions are different?
questions.explanation: M changes to N and the final 6 changes to 8, giving two differences.
